title: Kioxia and SanDisk 10th-Gen 332-Layer QLC NAND Achieves Industry's Highest Bit Density
event_hint: Kioxia and Sandisk unveil 10th-generation 332-layer QLC 3D flash memory at FMS 2026 (August 4, 2026), claiming the industry's highest bit density for QLC NAND.
problem: AI training, inference and hyperscale datacenter workloads drive unprecedented data growth, pressuring flash storage to deliver greater capacity, higher performance and improved energy efficiency simultaneously, while AI/cloud infrastructure faces power and cooling limits.
mechanism: CMOS directly Bonded to Array (CBA) architecture fabricates CMOS logic and the memory array on separate wafers then bonds them with high-precision wafer-to-wafer alignment; a 332-layer optimized floorplan raises bit density; Toggle DDR6.0 plus the Separate Command Address (SCA) protocol enables a faster interface; Power-Isolated Low-Tapped Termination (PI-LTT) improves I/O data-out transfer power efficiency.

evidence.claim: The 10th-gen QLC 3D flash delivers up to a 60% increase in bit density versus the 8th-generation, surpassing 37 Gb/mm^2, presented as the industry benchmark for QLC bit density.
evidence.condition: QLC; vendor survey as of August 3, 2026
evidence.source_locator: Press release lede + 'Key ... highlights' bullet - 332-layer architecture / bit density

evidence.claim: It is the industry's first QLC 3D flash memory technology to reach a 4.8 Gb/s NAND interface, enabled by Toggle DDR6.0 and the Separate Command Address (SCA) protocol.
evidence.condition: Vendor test environment (value may vary by use); 1 Gb/s = 1,000,000,000 bits/s
evidence.source_locator: Press release lede + 'Key ... highlights' bullet - 4.8 Gb/s NAND interface

evidence.claim: The new generation improves read and write bandwidth compared to the 8th-generation 3D flash memory.
evidence.source_locator: Press release lede - CBA technology paragraph

evidence.claim: CMOS-directly-Bonded-to-Array (CBA) architecture enhances density scaling, performance, and manufacturing efficiency; Power-Isolated Low-Tapped Termination (PI-LTT) improves I/O data-out transfer power efficiency.
evidence.condition: CBA: CMOS and cell array wafers manufactured separately then bonded; PI-LTT for I/O power
evidence.source_locator: 'Key ... highlights' bullets - CBA architecture and PI-LTT

evaluation_context: Joint Kioxia/Sandisk press release issued at Future of Memory and Storage (FMS) 2026, Santa Clara, August 4, 2026. 'Industry's highest' is a Kioxia/Sandisk survey claim as of August 3, 2026. Interface speed obtained under a vendor-specific test environment; no end-system or SSD-level benchmark results are provided.
limitations: No absolute die capacity (Gb), P/E endurance, write amplification, access latency, or absolute read/write bandwidth (GB/s) are given. No sampling or mass-production timing is stated (Kioxia says it will 'accelerate development toward the commercialization'). The PI-LTT power-efficiency gain is qualitative only (no multiplier or percentage). 'Industry's highest bit density' is a vendor self-survey claim.
project_relevance: Strongly relevant to storage_media density/bandwidth/power evidence: >37 Gb/mm^2 and a 4.8 Gb/s interface are concrete QLC density and interface advances, while CBA plus PI-LTT target the power/cooling constraints of AI infrastructure. However, missing endurance, absolute bandwidth and volume timing currently limit any assessment of deployable performance or cost/bit gain.
source_notes: 'Industry's highest bit density for QLC NAND' is a Kioxia/Sandisk self-survey as of August 3, 2026; 4.8 Gb/s measured under vendor-specific test environment.
